taxa.name: Australopithecus, species unresolved
taxa.meaning: Fossils assigned to Australopithecus without a secure species identification.
taxa.note: An indexing category, not a newly named species or a demonstrated ancestor.

evidence.title: Woranso-Mille: the MRD Australopithecus anamensis cranium
evidence.summary: A nearly complete cranium reveals the face of Australopithecus anamensis and adds to evidence that early australopith diversity cannot be reduced to a simple succession.
evidence.limits: Regional Woranso-Mille anchor; this specimen is distinct from the younger deyiremeda locality already mapped. An ancestor-descendant relationship is not demonstrated by the point. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published geological age of the fossil-bearing deposits.

evidence.title: Burtele: a foot with a grasping great toe
evidence.summary: The partial foot preserves a combination of bipedal and climbing adaptations different from the familiar Australopithecus afarensis pattern.
evidence.limits: Species assignment is unresolved in the cited original study; resemblance to Ardipithecus is not an identification. The map uses the Burtele research-area position. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published stratigraphic age, rounded to 3.4 Ma.

evidence.title: Lomekwi 3: large cores, hammerstones and anvils
evidence.summary: Excavated stone artifacts preserve intentional fracture and battering before the earliest currently identified Homo fossils.
evidence.limits: The maker is unknown. Nearby Kenyanthropus fossils do not identify the knappers; this tool locality is separate from the older fossil occurrence. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Stratigraphic, volcanic-marker and palaeomagnetic correlation in the original study.

evidence.title: Bokol Dora 1: early Oldowan flaking
evidence.summary: An excavated assemblage records systematic stone flaking in the Ledi-Geraru landscape.
evidence.limits: Broad Ledi-Geraru locality anchor. The earlier Homo mandible elsewhere in this research area does not prove who made these tools. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: The archaeological horizon is bracketed between 2.61 and 2.58 Ma.

evidence.title: East Gona: early Oldowan cores and flakes
evidence.summary: Sharp-edged flakes and cores document stone manufacture in the Afar Rift well before the classic Olduvai assemblages.
evidence.limits: One grouped East Gona anchor represents the published early assemblages. These are archaeological horizons, not a settlement occupied continuously throughout the bracket. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Volcanic ash and magnetic polarity constrain the archaeological deposits.

evidence.title: Lokalalei 2C: refitted stone-knapping sequences
evidence.summary: Matching discarded flakes back to their cores reveals controlled and repeated stone reduction.
evidence.limits: Refitting demonstrates manufacturing actions, not language, an ethnic identity, or a named species. The locality coordinate is rounded from the published position. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: The original study places the site at 2.34 ± 0.05 Ma; volcanic-marker correlation provides the chronology.

evidence.title: Kanjera South: recurring animal processing
evidence.summary: Cut-marked and broken animal remains occur in several Oldowan assemblages, supporting repeated access to carcasses.
evidence.limits: The combined strata span multiple episodes. Carcass processing does not establish a uniform diet, population size, or a single hunting method. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published stratigraphic age of the Kanjera South assemblages, approximately 2.0 Ma.

evidence.title: Garba IV E: an early Homo erectus jaw
evidence.summary: A child’s mandibular remains and dental analysis support an early Homo erectus attribution at a highland locality with Oldowan tools.
evidence.limits: The taxonomic attribution follows the cited analysis. Association within a layer does not identify the individual toolmaker. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Revised palaeomagnetic chronology for level E in the 2023 study.

evidence.title: Garba IV D: early Acheulean tools in the highlands
evidence.summary: Bifacial tools occur in the level above the mandible, extending the early Acheulean record in Ethiopia.
evidence.limits: This is a separate stratigraphic phase from level E. An industry is a technological classification, not a species or people. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Revised palaeomagnetic age of level D, approximately 1.95 Ma.

evidence.title: Kokiselei 4: early Acheulean large cutting tools
evidence.summary: Large cutting tools in West Turkana document an early Acheulean assemblage alongside a broader landscape of core-and-flake technology.
evidence.limits: The assemblage does not demonstrate that one technology replaced another everywhere, or identify a particular hominin maker. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Magnetostratigraphic dating of the enclosing sedimentary sequence.

evidence.title: Konso KGA6-A1: early Acheulean shaping
evidence.summary: The dated Konso sequence includes early large cutting tools with bifacial shaping.
evidence.limits: Regional Konso research-area anchor. Other Konso layers are younger; the whole sequence is not shown as a single continuous occupation. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Chronometric calibration assigns the KGA6-A1 Locus C assemblage approximately 1.75 Ma.

evidence.title: Konso: a shaped hippopotamus-bone handaxe
evidence.summary: A worked bone preserves deliberate flake removals and evidence interpreted as use, extending the known range of early tool materials.
evidence.limits: The specimen was recovered from the surface rather than excavated in an intact occupation floor. Its precise task and maker remain uncertain. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Surface specimen attributed to the approximately 1.4 Ma deposits of Konso.

evidence.title: Ewass Oldupa: Oldowan activity through changing environments
evidence.summary: Repeated archaeological horizons show early Olduvai tool use in changing river, lakeside and disturbed volcanic environments.
evidence.limits: Western Olduvai regional anchor. The broad span contains separate episodes and environmental changes; it does not imply unbroken residence. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified archaeological occurrences correlated with dated volcanic tuffs.

evidence.title: Olduvai T69: systematic knapped-bone tools
evidence.summary: A single horizon contains large mammal bones deliberately shaped by knapping, including elephant and hippopotamus material.
evidence.limits: An Olduvai basin anchor represents the T69 assemblage. Neither the bones nor nearby hominin fossils establish the identity of the makers. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: The excavated Bed II horizon is dated to approximately 1.5 Ma.

evidence.title: Nariokotome: the Turkana Boy skeleton
evidence.summary: The partial skeleton KNM-WT 15000 informs research on Homo erectus body form and development.
evidence.limits: A single individual is not a population estimate. Biological age and growth reconstructions depend on comparative assumptions. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Institutional specimen chronology gives an approximate age of 1.6 Ma.

evidence.title: Daka: Homo erectus in the Middle Awash
evidence.summary: A cranial vault and associated fossil discoveries extend the African Homo erectus record into the early Middle Pleistocene transition.
evidence.limits: Morphological similarity does not establish a mapped migration route or identify a direct ancestor of a living population. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: The Dakanihylo Member of the Bouri Formation is approximately 1.0 Ma.

evidence.title: Buia Uadi Aalad: an early Pleistocene Homo cranium
evidence.summary: A cranium from Eritrea preserves a mosaic of features relevant to variation within early Homo.
evidence.limits: The original report describes mixed erectus-like and sapiens-like traits. The map retains an unassigned category instead of treating it as early Homo sapiens. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: The fossil-bearing level is correlated near the end of the Jaramillo normal-polarity subchron.

evidence.title: Koobi Fora: different walking patterns on one surface
evidence.summary: A footprint surface preserves two distinct locomotor patterns, with comparisons suggesting more than one hominin form shared lakeside habitats.
evidence.limits: The study proposes Homo erectus and Paranthropus boisei, but tracks are not associated skeletons. The regional point does not specify an excavation square. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published age of the footprint-bearing Koobi Fora deposits, approximately 1.5 Ma.

evidence.title: Simbiro III: intensive obsidian biface production
evidence.summary: An unusually concentrated assemblage records skilled use of volcanic glass for bifacial tools in the Ethiopian highlands.
evidence.limits: The point is a minimum-age marker, not an exact occupation date. “Workshop” describes concentrated manufacture, not a modern production institution. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published lower-age constraint: more than 1.2 Ma; displayed at that threshold.

evidence.title: Gombore II-2: footprints beside a watering place
evidence.summary: Human and animal tracks preserve brief activity around a pond, alongside archaeological evidence of tool use and carcass processing.
evidence.limits: A footprint assemblage captures short events. Nearby older fossils do not securely identify the trackmakers; not every underlying artifact shares the footprint surface. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: The footprint surface is sealed by a volcanic tuff dated to approximately 700 ka.

evidence.title: Bodo: a Middle Pleistocene cranium
evidence.summary: The large cranium documents Middle Pleistocene human variation in the Ethiopian Rift.
evidence.limits: Homo heidelbergensis is used here as a disputed comparative label; alternative classifications exist for African fossils. Direct ancestry is not established. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Institutional specimen chronology gives an approximate age of 600 ka.

evidence.title: Olorgesailie: pigments and transported obsidian
evidence.dateLabel: About 320,000 to at least 295,000 years ago
evidence.summary: Middle Stone Age assemblages include coloring materials and obsidian moved from distant geological sources.
evidence.limits: Transport is observed through stone-source chemistry; social exchange is an interpretation. The date bracket groups sites and does not imply uninterrupted occupation. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Argon and uranium-series dating constrain a series of excavated sites.

evidence.title: Gademotta: pointed tools interpreted as projectiles
evidence.summary: Damage and shape analyses support the interpretation of some obsidian points as hafted hunting weapons.
evidence.limits: Delivery mechanisms are inferred from artifact damage. No preserved spear shaft identifies the exact weapon, and hunting equipment is not evidence of warfare. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Underlying archaeological deposits predate the approximately 279 ka marker; displayed at this minimum age.

evidence.title: Mieso: late Acheulean cleavers and biface manufacture
evidence.summary: Stratified assemblages at Mieso 7 and 31 preserve different stages of making and using large cutting tools.
evidence.limits: A grouped valley anchor represents distinct excavated clusters. Late Acheulean evidence overlaps the wider regional Middle Stone Age record. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Volcanic-tuff chronology, 0.212 ± 0.016 Ma, for the associated succession.

evidence.title: Aduma: points assessed as complex projectile tips
evidence.summary: Morphology, hafting traces and impact damage suggest changing weapon designs within the Aduma sequence.
evidence.limits: Spearthrower darts are a supported interpretation rather than preserved complete weapons. The broad Middle Awash anchor represents multiple localities. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published broad chronology for the later point-bearing phases.

evidence.title: Panga ya Saidi: the burial of a young child
evidence.summary: The articulated remains and surrounding sediments support deliberate interment of a young child in a filled grave.
evidence.limits: The evidence supports this burial; it does not establish a universal mortuary practice, named community, or belief system. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Luminescence-based burial chronology reported as 78.3 ± 4.1 ka.

evidence.title: Panga ya Saidi: changing tools in a coastal forest
evidence.summary: A shift toward smaller tools appears within a long, varied cave sequence rather than a single continent-wide technological transition.
evidence.limits: This boundary is a stratigraphic estimate. It does not establish a new ethnic group, sudden replacement, or the arrival date of humans on the coast. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Modeled age of the boundary between layers 17 and 16.

evidence.title: Shinfa-Metema 1: riverine foraging around the Toba eruption
evidence.summary: Animal remains document terrestrial and aquatic foods in a seasonal river setting; small points are interpreted as possible arrowheads.
evidence.limits: Bow use and river-assisted dispersal are hypotheses. This locality does not trace an actual journey out of Africa or establish a population bottleneck. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Youngest Toba Tuff cryptotephra correlates the occupation deposits to approximately 74 ka.

evidence.title: Fincha Habera: repeated highland occupation
evidence.summary: Stone tools, food remains and other occupation evidence show repeated use of a high-altitude rockshelter, including exploitation of giant mole-rats.
evidence.limits: The range contains repeated occupations, not proven permanent residence on every date. Cultural adaptation is not direct evidence of inherited high-altitude physiology. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published late Pleistocene occupation chronology.

evidence.title: Kisese II: early ostrich-eggshell bead production
evidence.summary: Beads and production debris document ornament manufacture within the shelter’s changing stone-tool sequence.
evidence.limits: Later burials and rock art are not assigned this early age. Bead similarity alone cannot identify ethnicity or a specific exchange network. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dates on ostrich eggshell constrain the early bead-bearing deposits.

evidence.title: Mumba VI-A: the late Kisele phase
evidence.summary: Luminescence dating constrains the latest Kisele assemblage.
evidence.limits: The industry label describes tools, not ancestry. The age range is dating uncertainty. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published quartz and feldspar luminescence chronology.

evidence.title: Mumba V: microliths and eggshell beads
evidence.summary: Late Mumba deposits contain small stone tools and ostrich-eggshell beads.
evidence.limits: This phase is distinct from earlier Kisele deposits; it does not imply continuous residence. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Luminescence age for the latest Mumba Industry deposits.

evidence.title: Mumba III: the Nasera technological phase
evidence.summary: Bed III contains numerous ostrich-eggshell beads and a later lithic assemblage.
evidence.limits: This is Mumba’s Nasera Industry phase, not the separate Nasera rockshelter. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published luminescence date for Bed III.

evidence.title: Porc-Epic Cave: varied ochre-processing techniques
evidence.summary: Grinding and pounding equipment preserves different ways of producing pigments from iron-rich rocks.
evidence.limits: The exact uses of the powders are not established. Functional and symbolic uses may overlap; colors do not identify an ethnic group. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Approximate published chronology of the ochre-bearing Middle Stone Age levels.

evidence.title: Lukenya Hill: the KNM-LH 1 human cranium
evidence.summary: A partial cranial vault contributes evidence of human anatomical diversity during the Last Glacial Maximum.
evidence.limits: The chronology dates the fossil’s archaeological context, not the bone directly. Shape differences are not a diagnosis of a modern ethnic population. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Revised AMS radiocarbon chronology from associated ostrich eggshell dates.

evidence.title: Kuumbi Cave: late Pleistocene coastal occupation
evidence.summary: Quartz microliths, cut-marked animal bones and marine food remains provide clear evidence of occupation near the end of the Pleistocene.
evidence.limits: Earlier claims of a pre-20 ka occupation remain disputed. Lower sea level connected Zanzibar to the mainland; these finds do not establish an ocean crossing. The point is a rounded cave locality, not an excavation square.
evidence.dateBasis: The reinvestigation places the onset of relatively regular occupation at approximately 17–19 ka cal BP, with complex redeposition and dating limitations.

evidence.title: Uraha: the UR 501 Homo mandible
evidence.summary: The fragmentary mandible extends the early Homo record into the Malawi Rift.
evidence.limits: The Homo rudolfensis attribution is comparative and debated. This is a locality anchor near Uraha, not the precise recovery position; it is not the oldest known Homo today. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Faunal correlation places the fossil near 2.4 Ma; a broad 2.5–2.3 Ma bracket retains regional chronological uncertainty.

evidence.title: Malema RC 11: a Paranthropus maxillary fragment
evidence.summary: A jaw fragment with teeth documents a robust-chewing hominin in northern Malawi.
evidence.limits: Attribution to Paranthropus boisei is qualified. A taxon at this locality does not demonstrate continuous occupation between the better-known eastern and southern African fossil regions. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Biostratigraphic correlation places the Chiwondo Beds specimen near 2.4 Ma.

evidence.title: Karonga: early dated Chitimwe archaeological deposits
evidence.summary: Dated sediments preserve Middle Stone Age artifacts within an extensively surveyed landscape beside northern Lake Malawi.
evidence.limits: Regional research-area anchor, not a single excavation. It records preservation of archaeology, not first human arrival; later fire and vegetation changes require a separate causal interpretation. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Optically stimulated luminescence constrains the earliest preserved archaeological sedimentation to approximately 92 ± 7 ka.

evidence.title: Chaminade I: late Middle Stone Age activity
evidence.summary: Two artifact concentrations show flexible stone reduction in a riverside setting near Karonga.
evidence.limits: The interval combines activity and burial of deposits. It does not show continuous residence or a linear increase in technological complexity. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Published contextual span; most artifacts are in deposits near 41 ka, with burial by alluvial-fan aggradation by about 21 ka.

evidence.title: Chaminade II: a slowly accumulating archaeological landscape
evidence.dateLabel: Older than about 47,000 to older than about 17,000 years ago
evidence.summary: Stone artifacts occur within an alluvial fan affected by slow deposition and partial erosion.
evidence.limits: Displayed endpoints are chronological thresholds. Separate phases and erosion prevent reading the entire span as uninterrupted occupation or a precise abandonment date. Coordinates are rounded locality anchors, not excavation GPS.
evidence.dateBasis: Luminescence, sedimentology and micromorphology bracket activity from >47 to >17 ka in the published study.

evidence.title: Namorotukunan NMT1: early Oldowan manufacture
evidence.summary: Cores and flakes document stone working in the oldest of three excavated horizons.
evidence.limits: Maker unknown. This is one dated horizon, not continuous residence. Published locality coordinate is shared across the excavations.
evidence.dateBasis: Stratigraphic and palaeomagnetic placement; approximate age. Figure 4 identifies NMT1 within unit C1-S3.

evidence.title: Namorotukunan NMT2: tools and animal processing
evidence.summary: Stone artifacts and cutmarked animal bone occur in the middle horizon.
evidence.limits: The paper gives about 2.60 Ma in its chronology and Figure 4, but 2.58 Ma elsewhere; this span preserves that discrepancy. Maker unknown.
evidence.dateBasis: NMT2 lies near the Gauss–Matuyama reversal; approximate stratigraphic age, not a measured occupation duration.

evidence.title: Namorotukunan NMT3: a younger Oldowan horizon
evidence.summary: A younger excavated assemblage preserves stone-tool production.
evidence.limits: Artifact orientation and missing smaller pieces indicate some post-depositional disturbance. Maker unknown.
evidence.dateBasis: Approximate stratigraphic age of unit C3, above the Gauss–Matuyama reversal.

evidence.title: Lee Adoyta LD 760: an unresolved australopith
evidence.summary: Associated teeth represent an Australopithecus individual whose species remains unresolved.
evidence.limits: Surface recovery is assigned to a fossil-bearing unit below the dated tuff. The plotted threshold is not an exact fossil age. Rounded basin anchor from Figure 1.
evidence.dateBasis: Table 1 reports >2.63 Ma; the overlying Lee Adoyta Tuff is 2.631 ± 0.011 Ma.

evidence.title: Asboli AS 100: early Homo molars
evidence.summary: Two molars provide a separate early Homo occurrence in the Ledi-Geraru research area.
evidence.limits: Species assignment remains unresolved. Fossils do not establish a settlement or identify nearby toolmakers. Rounded Asboli anchor from Figure 1.
evidence.dateBasis: The fossil horizon is immediately below the Giddi Sands Tuff, dated 2.593 ± 0.006 Ma.

evidence.title: Gona DAN5: Homo erectus and varied stone tools
evidence.summary: Cranial remains occur with Oldowan and Acheulean artifacts.
evidence.limits: Some cranial pieces and artifacts were in situ; many others were surface finds with weaker contextual assurance. Rounded Figure 1 map position.
evidence.dateBasis: Estimated from sedimentation within a wider 1.78–1.07 Ma palaeomagnetic bracket; not a direct fossil date.

evidence.title: Gona BSN12: a younger erectus cranial occurrence
evidence.summary: A partial cranium and both Oldowan and Acheulean tools are associated with the Boolihinan Tuff.
evidence.limits: Tuff adhering to fossils and tools strengthens their association; unrelated surface artifacts are less secure. Rounded Figure 1 map position.
evidence.dateBasis: Geochemical correlation to a 1.262 ± 0.034 Ma tuff, supported by palaeomagnetism; uncertainty is 1 sigma.
